title: The Boy Who Painted Dreams
author: Hamidreza Rostami
moral_lesson: Imagination belongs to the person who makes it, and the worlds you create are always waiting for you to come back.
short_description: A boy whose paintbrush starts to shimmer paints a door into a dream world made of his own pictures.
long_description: Leo loves to paint so much that his bedroom is covered in pictures, right up to the ceiling. One night, painting a starry sky above his bed, he feels his brush change: the bristles shimmer with stardust, and the stars he paints lift off the ceiling and become real. Soon a crescent moon hangs in the air, clouds drift through the room, and a tiny lit cottage with a smoking chimney sits on his dresser. Then Leo has a big idea, and paints a real wooden door. Beyond it waits a world of talking animals, flying fish, candy trees and lemonade rivers, all of it made from his own paintings and all of it delighted to meet him. When the night ends, his creations promise to wait for him, and Leo learns that the magic was real all along, and it was his.
visual_style: High-quality 3D animated children's illustration (cinematic children's animation), dreamy painterly rendering, glowing starlight and soft magical gradients, rich night blues against bright paint colours

art_direction.character_lock: Leo is identical on every page: about seven, messy dark brown hair sticking up at the back, big warm brown eyes, light freckles, gap-toothed grin, paint-splattered BLUE t-shirt, dark navy shorts, and MISMATCHED SOCKS - one red, one blue, with NO shoes.
art_direction.creature_lock: The purple elephant is small and round with big floppy ears, tiny sparkling silver wings and amber eyes. The giraffe is green with darker green polka dots and a long neck. The flying turtle is round and green with big feathered wings.
art_direction.punctuation_rule: Dialogue uses double quotation marks throughout. Narrative prose carries no quotation marks. Contractions are rewritten out (do not, did not, it is) so no stray apostrophes appear.
art_direction.paragraph_rule: The back cover blurb is set in three clearly separated paragraphs with a visible blank gap between them, in normal mixed case.
